title: 20-Mile March
equation: Long-term Output = Daily Floor × Days Hit per Year × Years
hook: Huge months followed by dead months isn't growth. It's a rollercoaster, and it wears everyone out.
statement: Hit the same steady performance target every period, whether times are good or bad.
explainer: Racing on good days and resting on bad ones feels smart but loses long races. A floor you never miss gives you growth you can actually predict and plan around.
sop: Pick a number you'll hit every single period.
Commit to never missing that floor.
Cap the heroic overperformance so you don't burn out.
Review your pace, not your best month.
equation_example: Daily Floor $500, hit on 347 of 365 days, about 95%, for 5 years. $500 × 347 × 5 = $867,500. Higher consistency over more years means steady, predictable growth. Lower means you're relying on heroics instead of a system.
question: Write down your monthly minimum, then count how many months this year you actually hit it.
closing_statement: Pace beats heroics over a long haul.
caption:
Principle Nº 277: 20-Mile March

Huge months followed by dead months isn't growth. It's a rollercoaster, and it wears everyone out.

Hit the same steady performance target every period, whether times are good or bad.

Your turn: Write down your monthly minimum, then count how many months this year you actually hit it.
